findings.message: After this fix, employment periods are read through the viewer's hr data scope (`listEmploymentPeriods(tx, v, ids)`), but team membership and allocation totals are still read without that scope. When a team member falls outside the viewer's hr scope, hr returns no period for them. `fteIn` then returns 0, so the person is treated as 'not employed'. They drop out of capacity, demand and bench with no sign that anything was hidden, so 'could not see' reads the same as 'nothing there'. The grid has the same root cause: `gridIn` (grid.ts:25) filters people through `listPeople(tx, v, { ids })` while `peopleIn` keeps every allocation, so hidden people vanish and the screen shows 'No allocations yet'. Fix: decide what a narrow-scope viewer should see. Either compute the team aggregates (capacity, demand, bench) from an unscoped, system read and mask only the person-level fields, or return an explicit `hidden: n` / 'partial' flag that the screen and MCP show. Add a variant test with at least three viewers (Leadership, PM, an HR viewer limited to Australia) so that dropping or keeping the scoping changes the result. The current tests only use maya as Leadership or PM, and they pass with or without the scoping.
findings.scenario: An HR user scoped to Australia only (hr shows them 14 people; HR is granted allocations:read) opens /allocations → the Delivery team (Sri Lanka) capacity and demand read about 0 instead of 140..144, the January bench is empty, and the 'Everyone' grid shows 'No allocations yet' even though about 140 FTE of allocations exist.

findings.message: `mayAllocate` returns true whenever `viewerOf(ctx)` is missing (`!v || can(...)`). A ServiceContext without a viewer, such as a job, agent or contract-command context, skips the project-scope check entirely. `copyMonth` inherits this through its `allowed` filter. When the viewer is missing, this should deny or require an explicit system actor that is checked by kind, not grant unscoped allocation.
findings.scenario: allocate is called with a contextFor.job(tenant, ...) context or any context without `viewer` and { person: 'LL-0417', projectKey: 'FLT', ... } → the write succeeds on a project the caller does not manage. With a PM viewer, the same input is rejected with a data-scope error.

findings.message: When `through` is earlier than `month`, `monthsBetween` returns only `[from]`. The reversed range is accepted without error and only one month is written. The range is also unbounded. Fix: add a `.refine` that `through >= month` and cap the span, for example at 24 months.
findings.scenario: allocate({ person: 'Kasun Dias', projectKey: 'CON', month: '2027-03', through: '2027-01', percent: 40 }) → only March 2027 is written and the call reports success; the user meant Jan–Mar or made a typo and gets no error. through: '2099-12' → about 870 rows inserted in one call.

findings.message: `personOf` now resolves the person through the caller's hr scope. A person who exists but sits outside the caller's hr scope gets the error 'no person X', which reads as if they don't exist. Fix: raise a scope error that names the reason.
findings.scenario: A PM whose hr scope excludes LL-0500 calls allocate({ person: 'LL-0500', ... }) → 'no person LL-0500' instead of a data-scope error.

findings.message: The current month is taken from Postgres `current_date` (the DB session timezone). The rest of the module uses the app's `today` (`windowMonths`, `isForecast`). Near a month boundary the @assigned scope and the screens can name different months. Fix: pass in the app's date.
findings.scenario: On 2026-11-01 at 03:00 Sri Lanka time, the DB date (UTC) is still 2026-10-31 → assignedProjects uses October allocations while the screens show November.

findings.message: The default team name 'Delivery team' is written out separately in services.ts (copyMonth input default), forecast.ts:50, actions.ts:11 and the migration defaults, alongside `TEAM` in fixtures/plan.ts. Fix: use one exported constant.

The comment says the read is 'for this one user', but the code reads the whole active people directory with a system job context and then filters in JS. Fix: look the person up by userId (or use a contract read by user) so the system-privileged read covers only that user.

`retention: []` with the claim 'no personal fields'. `allocations.member` (person_id, skill) and `allocations.allocation` (person_id, month, percent) are per-person records about identifiable employees. Under module-standard.md, every personal-data table needs a 032 retention entry. Fix: add retention rules, for example purging rows for leavers, or document why these tables are not personal data.

`currentViewer()` can return null, and `ctxFor(viewer)` then throws a TypeError instead of a clear unauthenticated error. It still fails closed. Fix: check for a null viewer before building the context.
findings.scenario: A signed-out POST to copyMonthAction → 500 TypeError ('Cannot read properties of null') instead of an auth error.

findings.message: This round makes allocations read the hr contract with the caller's data scope ('scoped hr v2 contract'). Its own published contract reads, `listAllocations` and `personMonthTotals`, still take no caller context and return every person's allocations in the tenant. architecture.md says cross-module reads go through contract functions 'which apply the caller's data scope', and the same class was already fixed in hr. Fix: give the contract reads a ServiceContext/Viewer parameter, filter by the caller's scope (for example managed/assigned projects or the people the caller may see), and version the contract (v2) with a README note.
findings.scenario: Another module (for example time or chat) calls listAllocations(tx, {from:'2026-10-01', to:'2027-03-01'}) for an Engineer viewer. It gets every person's monthly allocations across all projects, not only what that viewer may see.
